question: On the medium prime tier (the ten generic prime-order curves at log2 r 32-49 of research/prime_medium_tier_rho_20261107), what is the pooled paired rho.plain / rho.negation operation-count ratio at w = 0, does its 95% interval exclude 1.2 from below, and is it consistent with sqrt 2 = 1.414 or with the 2026-11-07 point value of about 1.285?

claims.text: Every admitted run recovers the planted logarithm and every measured run replays exactly (pod verify --replay-all and a local re-audit).

The pooled curve-equal ratio theta = mean S(rho.plain) / mean S(rho.negation) at w = 0 is classified by the PROTOCOL.md section 9 table as confirm_sqrt2, exceeds_1.2_below_sqrt2, exceeds_sqrt2, below_1.2 or inconclusive.
claims.if_supported: report the verdict and theta with its interval; the 2026-11-07 P4 stays inconclusive (this study does not re-decide it)

claims.text: The estimator and harness resolve a known ratio: bsgs.textbook / bsgs.negation, expected 1.5 (methods::expected_s), on the same curves, with its 95% interval excluding 1.2 from below and 1.5 inside its 99% interval.

Where theta falls short of sqrt 2, the shortfall is attributed (secondary, predeclared) to charged negation-map overhead (look-ahead additions, escape doublings, set-up, starts, verification) or to the walk itself (theta_steps below sqrt 2), with a size trend and the look-ahead heuristic sqrt2/(1+1/32) reported beside it.
Nothing here is a statement about cryptographic sizes, wall-clock speed-up of the negation map, or a lower bound on ECDLP; it is not a new IC result and changes no leaderboard row.

hypotheses.statement: At these sizes ecbench's rho.negation saves less than sqrt 2 in charged operations over rho.plain: theta is about 1.30, its interval excludes 1.2 from below and lies below sqrt 2.
hypotheses.mechanism: rho.plain sits near its floor (R about 1.01) while rho.negation pays the Wiener-Zuccherato look-ahead (about 1/32 extra additions per step, charged), cycle escapes and possibly a larger walk-randomness penalty of a 16-jump r-adding walk on classes

predictions.minimum_effect: point about 1.30; 95% interval inside [1.20, 1.414): verdict exceeds_1.2_below_sqrt2

literature.ref: Wiener and Zuccherato, Faster attacks on elliptic curve cryptosystems, SAC 1998
literature.claim: the negation map halves the classes, an ideal sqrt 2 saving in expected steps, and fruitless cycles appear; the look-ahead against 2-cycles

literature.ref: Bos, Kleinjung and Lenstra, On the use of the negation map in the Pollard rho method, ANTS IX 2010
literature.claim: with r-adding walks, fruitless cycles and their handling make the practical negation-map gain smaller than sqrt 2

literature.ref: Bernstein, Lange and Schwabe, On the correct use of the negation map in the Pollard rho method, PKC 2011
literature.claim: fruitless-cycle frequency for additive walks with r jumps (2-cycles about 1/(2r) per step without look-ahead, 4-cycles about (r-1)/(4 r^3)); with enough jumps and cheap cycle handling the gain approaches sqrt 2

literature.ref: Teske, On random walks for Pollard's rho method, Math. Comp. 2001

rho.negation: 16 jumps for r above 2^22, distinguished-point bits floor(bits(r)/4), look-ahead on, a 16-point cycle window with escape by doubling the least-key point, abandon on re-entry, no Brent detection, walk cap 20*2^dp+64 steps; every addition and doubling charged, canonicalisations uncharged

power.note: analysis/power.json, from the OLD run's variance only: curve-centred per-run CV 0.41 (rho-neg) and 0.56 (rho-plain), pair correlation -0.22 [-0.43, 0.02] over 80 workloads; the delta method reproduces the old J1 half-width (0.113 vs 0.1135 observed). Target: 95% half-width <= 0.05, because sqrt 2 - 1.285 = 0.129 > 2 x 0.05 (one interval cannot contain both references) and 1.285 - 0.05 > 1.2. 10 curves x 36 targets x 6 rounds = 2160 pairs: delta-method half-width 0.041 at theta 1.285 and 0.046 at sqrt 2 at rho -0.22 (0.045 / 0.049 at rho -0.43). Simulation (200 designs x 2000 resamples per truth, lognormal pairs): median half-width 0.041-0.048, P(half-width <= 0.05) 0.75-1.00, coverage 0.93-0.955; truth 1.285 gives exceeds_1.2_below_sqrt2 with probability 0.965-0.98 (else inconclusive), truth sqrt 2 gives confirm_sqrt2 with probability 0.935. With rho at its lower end 2094 pairs reach 0.05 at sqrt 2, hence 36 targets per curve (2160 pairs). The 1.2 decision is a single interval (no correction); the split-half A/A uses Bonferroni over two (97.5% intervals).

secondary.name: theta at w = 0.1 and w = 1

stopping_rules.rule: ten jobs (M1-M9, PC), each once; fixed N; PC first
a per-execution timeout (300 s) or exhaustion is a censored row kept in the session; more than 1% censored in any arm makes the verdict inconclusive

an incomplete session (Spot loss, launcher failure, job timeout) is kept and rerun once under a new job name with the identical spec; a second failure leaves that job out; the analysis runs on the completed sessions and is inconclusive if fewer than 90% of the planned 2160 pairs are complete
a complete session with a passing audit is admitted for counts even if the pod's L2 wall gate failed (exit 42/43); no wall time is reported

decision_rule.text: PROTOCOL.md section 9. Gates G1 (every session complete, its audit ok with replay-all, frozen binary and spec ids), G2 (rho-neg-aa counts identical to rho-neg in every pair), G3 (positive control: bsgs-tb/bsgs-neg 95% lower end above 1.2 and 1.5 inside its 99% interval, its A/A identical), G4 (split-half A/A: even/odd ratios of rho-neg and rho-plain each with 1 inside the 97.5% interval), G5 (censoring at most 1% per arm), G6 (at least 90% of planned pairs). If any gate fails: inconclusive. Otherwise, with [L, U] the 95% interval of theta: L > 1.2 and L <= sqrt 2 <= U: confirm_sqrt2; L > 1.2 and U < sqrt 2: exceeds_1.2_below_sqrt2; L > sqrt 2: exceeds_sqrt2; U < 1.2: below_1.2; otherwise (1.2 inside [L, U]): inconclusive. Reported beside it, never changing it: whether 1.285 lies inside [L, U], whether the half-width is at most 0.05, and the section 9a secondaries. Tie-break: an endpoint within 0.002 of 1.2 or sqrt 2 is recomputed with 200000 resamples (seed tag analysis/bootstrap-large) and that interval decides.
decision_rule.threshold: 1.2 (lower end of the 95% interval) and sqrt 2
decision_rule.statistic: curve-equal ratio of mean S, w = 0
decision_rule.interval: stratified (by curve) workload-cluster bootstrap, 20000 resamples, seed from seeds.json tag analysis/bootstrap, percentile type 7
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: theta and its distance to sqrt 2 and to 1.285
